page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.4xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 64 GB of DDR4 memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor running at a base clock of 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance integrates 35 MB of L3 cache along with instruction set support for AVX-512 with VNNI. The instance features 600 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, with no included discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate a balanced profile across multi-threaded applications, though single-core throughput is comparatively constrained. Multi-threaded evaluations such as the PassMark CPU score at 14,384.81, Geekbench multi-core at 7,072.0, and stress-ng multi-core place the instance in the middle 50% tier. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,132.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,285.68, place it in the lower 25% bracket. Memory throughput registers at 88.17 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 46.6 GB/sec for write operations.

The inclusion of 600 GB NVMe local storage and 16 Gbps baseline networking enhances data throughput for I/O-sensitive applications without requiring additional networked storage overhead. While single-thread instruction throughput shows performance tradeoffs against newer hardware generations, its aggregate thread count, dedicated core allocation, and large cache volume maintain stable throughput under sustained operational loads.

The hardware configuration suits balanced enterprise workloads that benefit from integrated local high-speed storage. Appropriate use cases include relational database hosting, Redis key-value caching (scoring 13.2 million SET operations per second), static web serving, CI/CD automated build pipelines, and extract, transform, load (ETL) processing queues.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.4xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores), 64 GB of DDR4 RAM, and 600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz, it supports AVX-512 VNNI instructions and provides a 16 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate balanced multi-core execution, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 14,384.81 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,072.0, though single-threaded performance lands in the lower 25% distribution. With uncached memory read bandwidth of 88.17 GB/sec and local NVMe storage included, this instance provides predictable I/O density for multi-threaded services. It is technically appropriate for mid-tier database hosting, distributed caching layers such as Redis, CI/CD pipelines, and general enterprise application hosting requiring local scratch storage.
